mainEntity.name: Why is My Water Heater Making Noise?
mainEntity.text: Why is My Water Heater Making Noise?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hearing strange noises from your water heater can be unsettling, but often, it's a common issue that plumbers see all the time. One of the most frequent culprits for rumbling or popping sounds is sediment buildup at the bottom of the tank. Over time, minerals like calcium and magnesium from your water supply settle, and when the heating element turns on, these sediments heat up and create steam bubbles, which then burst, causing those popping or rumbling sounds. Another type of noise, a high-pitched whine or whistling, could indicate an issue with the heating element itself, or possibly a restricted water flow. If you hear banging or knocking, it might be due to water hammer in your pipes, which can be exacerbated by issues with your water heater's internal components. Loud cracking sounds are less common but could point to expansion and contraction issues within the tank or a heating element. While some sediment buildup is normal, excessive amounts can reduce your water heater’s efficiency and shorten its lifespan, making it work harder. Understanding these sounds is key to knowing when to call in the pros. If the noises are persistent, very loud, or accompanied by other problems like leaks or a lack of hot water, it’s definitely time to have a professional take a look.
